The 1H NMR data shows four signals integrating to 1H, 1H, 3H, and 3H, totaling 8 hydrogens. This matches propenyl acetate (CH₃COOCH=CHCH₃), whereas butenyl acetate would have an additional CH₂ group (10 hydrogens total). The alkene proton signals appear at 7.0 ppm (d, J = 16.0 Hz) and 5.5 ppm (dq). The large coupling constant of 16.0 Hz is characteristic of a trans double bond (cis typically 6–12 Hz). The downfield proton at 7.0 ppm is attached to the oxygen-bearing carbon, and the 5.5 ppm proton shows dq splitting from both the trans alkene proton and the adjacent methyl group. The methyl singlet at 2.1 ppm corresponds to the acetate methyl, and the doublet at 1.6 ppm corresponds to the propenyl methyl. All data are consistent with trans-propenyl acetate.

Answer: B
